senses.gloss:
Lepākṣi
([village of] the blinded eye’)
------------------------------------------
Lepākṣi is one of the 108 important Śivakṣetras (holy place dedicated to god शिव) mentioned in the Skandapurāṇa. Its temple is said to have been established by the great sage अगस्त्य himself.
The present लेपाक्षि is a small village which lies 14.5 kms. (9 miles) east of Hindupur in the Ananthapur district of Andhra Pradesh. The original temple might have been built in the 7th century A. D.
लेपाक्षि">Vīrabhadra Temple at LepākṣiIts famous temple of वीरभद्र lies on a low rocky hill called Kūrmaśilā because it is shaped like a कूर्म or tortoise. It was constructed by Virūpaṇṇa (the treasurer of Vijayanagara empire) during the 16th century. Since he constructed the temple from the State funds without the permission of the king, he was punished by plucking out his eyes, which, he did, himself!
The temple campus has four shrines dedicated to वीरभद्र (the terrible deity who destroyed दक्ष’s sacrifice), Pāpanāśeśvara-शिव, Śrī राम and दुर्गा.
There are very good sculptured images of Anantaśayana (Viṣṇu), Dattā-treya, ब्रह्मा, the sage नारद, Rambhā (a celestial nymph) and Virūpaṇṇa (the builder).
The nāṭyamaṇḍapa is decorated with exquisitely sculptured pillars having life size images of musicians and dancers.
The kalyaṇamaṇḍapa is unfinished.
Bas-reliefs on the outer walls and mural paintings with vegetable dyes on the inner walls are very attractive. They depict stories from the epics and the पुराणस्.
At a distance of 180 metres (600 ft.) to the east of the temple, there is a colossal नन्दि, said to be the largest in India. It is carved out of a monolithic rock. It is 6 metres (20 ft.) in height and 9 metres (30 ft.) in length.
